NVDA.rationale: NVDA's fundamental health is elite: Q3 FY2026 revenue of $57.01B with 63.2% operating margin, 73.4% gross margin, and $31.91B net income represent among the highest-quality earnings in large-cap tech history. The balance sheet is a fortress ($8.47B debt vs $118.9B equity, D/E 0.071x) and three-quarter OCF of $66.53B confirms massive cash generation. The franchise moat—80-92% data center GPU share, CUDA ecosystem with 5.9M developers, annual architecture cadence—is the strongest in semiconductor history, and hyperscaler capex continues to rise (Meta raised to $125-145B). However, valuation is the binding constraint: at 56.5x trailing PE, NVDA sits above the median of its own one-year range (~51x) and well above the 43.2x trough, with only a 1.8% earnings yield against a 4.40% 10-year. Price has consolidated for two quarters while earnings surged ~47%, implying the market has absorbed growth rather than re-rated. The near-term catalyst (May 20 earnings, consensus $1.70 EPS) is real but historically has produced post-earnings declines in 5 of 7 quarters, and the helium supply disruption (30% of global production offline) poses a tangible Blackwell shipment risk. Custom silicon competition (Amazon Trainium $20B ARR, Broadcom $73B backlog) is growing but remains fragmented. Net margin compression from 55.0% to 52.4% over the trailing year warrants monitoring. The score reflects a world-class business whose stock is priced for continued perfection, with limited margin of safety and macro headwinds (oil shock, rising rates) that compress the equity risk premium.
